subject: Order Form: off-ramp cadence & mutual opt-out playbook
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-06-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form draft — off-ramp timing and termination mechanics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sharing the draft Order Form earlier this week. Procurement has a couple of gating items before we can move to signature: primarily around end-of-term mechanics and the auto-renew window. High-level asks from Acme: 

- Mutual termination-for-convenience option (limited scope) — we want a path for both sides to walk away without cause in certain scenarios.
- Clarify notice timing for opt-outs (we prefer 60 days but would consider 90 with other concessions).
- Sync the auto-renew opt-out window so it aligns with procurement calendar (our renewal notices are typically 45–60 days).
- Transition commitments (what Redwood will provide if we exercise an off-ramp): data export, KV cache handoff, limited runbook support.

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_Draft.pdf (redlines inline). Can your team provide a short playbook that explains how Redwood handles off-ramps (notice windows, pro-rata credits, transition support, and any limitations)? We want to present something to finance/legal on our side next week.

Also cc'd Tom in case there are technical questions on the transition obligations.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we get a proposed playbook and redline summary by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Connors
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloud
[Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — off-ramp timing and termination mechanics

Sarah — thanks, and good questions. Putting a short playbook and a recommended set of concession options together — summary below, then I’ll attach a concise PDF for your procurement/legal.

Quick summary (Redwood recommended):
- Mutual termination-for-convenience: possible, but constrained. Recommend: mutual TFC limited to Order Forms <= $100k or pilot agreements; larger deals remain company-termination only.
- Notice window: offer 60-day customer opt-out by default; if Acme requests 90 days, we’d request a 45–60 day invoice finalization period and an extended transition SLA (up to 90 days) at additional cost.
- Auto-renew opt-out: propose a 45-day opt-out window before renewal; customer must provide written notice.
- Transition support: include a 30-day standard transition package (data export, API keys revocation plan, a one-day runbook call); extended support available as paid professional services.
- Credits: pro-rata credits for prepaid months; no additional termination fee for mutual TFC within the constrained scope above.

Next steps:
1) I’ll attach Redwood_Offramp_Playbook_v1.pdf with the language we typically provide to Procurement.
2) Ben — can you and Kimberly review and flag any legal/procurement risk items? Marissa, please confirm whether we can offer mutual TFC at the pilot tier.
3) Sarah — if this looks directionally OK, can you share the internal timeline for legal review? You mentioned wanting this next week — we can prioritize.

Naomi Feldman
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Offramp_Playbook_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — off-ramp timing and termination mechanics

Naomi — quick redline notes from legal/procurement perspective after reading the playbook:

- Mutual TFC: Legal prefers limiting mutual termination for convenience to pilots and proof-of-concept Order Forms under a $100k TCV threshold. For >$100k deals, we should retain company-only TFC but can offer enhanced transition SLAs and credits.
- Notice windows: 60-day customer opt-out is acceptable. We should not agree to a 90-day customer notice without pricing concessions or a transition fee.
- Auto-renew: 45-day opt-out window aligns with our billing cadence; require written notice to Redwood support + account team.
- Transition obligations: keep the standard 30-day handoff (data export + two runbook calls). Offer extended 60/90-day assistance as billable professional services, with a defined scope (X hours, identified deliverables).
- Wording: add explicit limitation on liability for net-new models and any customer-managed on-prem components (we're only obligated for data export and runbook, not re-architecting customer infra).

If we agree on the limited mutual TFC for pilots, I support moving that language to the next redline. Marissa — can you confirm sales ok for the pilot carve?

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-06-11T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form draft — off-ramp timing and termination mechanics

Naomi / Ben / Kimberly / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. Acme is generally comfortable with the approach below provided a few clarifications are made in the contract language:

- Mutual TFC: acceptable for pilot Order Forms up to $100k TCV. Please add the explicit $100k threshold to the Order Form.
- Notice windows: we can accept a 60-day opt-out and a 45-day auto-renew opt-out window. Please add a sample notice template.
- Transition support: the standard 30-day package is fine; we’d like one additional runbook call (so two total) and a documented data export checklist.
- Liability carve: understood — please add a short paragraph clarifying that transition obligations exclude customer-managed on-prem components.

If you can turn these edits into a redline and a DocuSign-ready Order Form, procurement aims to complete internal approvals by June 25. Attached is our Procurement_Checklist.xlsx for your intake team.

Can you confirm Redwood’s timeline to produce the final redline and the DocuSign envelope?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Connors
Head of Procurement, Acme Cloud
